The eldest son of Henry the Fowler, this 10th-century king unified the German tribes and became Holy Roman Emperor in 962 after installing family members in the realm's most powerful duchies — who was he?
Otto the Great: Holy Roman Emperor from 962 to 973.
Hailed by the historian Thucydides as 'the first citizen of Athens,' this statesman transformed the Delian League into an Athenian empire during the city's Golden Age — who is he?
In the Book of Genesis, this unnamed woman falsely accused Joseph of assault after he spurned her advances, landing him in prison — later Islamic tradition names her Zuleikha. Who is she?
Potiphar's wife: Figure from Jewish and Muslim tradition.
An Indian politician born in 1970, this member of the Indian National Congress serves as the 12th leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha and represents Rae Bareli. Who is he?
Rahul Gandhi: 12th Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha since 2024.
He made his film debut as the boozy title character in a 1987 comedy, then decades later earned an Oscar nomination for playing Jack Hock in Can You Ever Forgive Me? — who is he?
Born in Newcastle upon Tyne to Russian émigré parents, this KGB spy ring leader in New York was arrested by the FBI on espionage charges in 1957 — who was he?
Prince Gustaf Adolf, Duke of Västerbotten

In July 1984, a lone gunman killed 22 people at a fast-food restaurant in a Southern California border town before a police sniper ended his 77-minute rampage — for years it held the record as the deadliest such attack by a single gunman in U.S. history. What is this event known as?
San Ysidro McDonald's massacre: 1984 mass shooting in California, U.S.
Known until 2003 as the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, this Balkan union dissolved in 2006 when its junior partner voted for independence — which two-republic state?
Serbia and Montenegro: Country in Southeast Europe (1992–2006)

Defended by weapons designed by the polymath Archimedes, this Roman conquest of a Sicilian city in 213–212 BC ended with the inventor's death at a soldier's hands despite orders to spare him — which historic clash?
Siege of Syracuse (213–212 BC): Roman victory during the Second Punic War.

Daughter of Darius III of Persia, she was captured after her father's defeat at Issus and became the second bride of the Macedonian conqueror at the Susa weddings in 324 BC, before being killed by his other spouse, Roxana — who was she?
Stateira (wife of Alexander the Great): Daughter of Darius III, died 323 BC.

Fought from 1992 to 1997, this Central Asian conflict pitted rebels from the Garm and Gorno-Badakhshan regions, organized as the United Tajik Opposition, against a Russian-backed government — which conflict was it?
Tajikistani Civil War: Armed conflict in Tajikistan from 1992 to 1997.
He landed at Anzac Cove in 1915, distinguished himself planning the Battle of Pozières, and remains the only Australian ever to reach the rank of field marshal — who was he?
An economist who entered parliament via a 1981 by-election, this Samoan politician went on to serve as his country's prime minister from 1998 all the way to 2021 — who is he?
Tuilaʻepa Saʻilele Malielegaoi: Prime Minister of Samoa from 1998 to 2021. After Tofilau resigned in 1998, Tuilaʻepa became the prime minister and HRPP party leader.
This American private equity investor and retired naval officer completed the Explorers Grand Slam and then dove to the deepest point of all five oceans during a 2018–19 expedition. Who is he?
Beginning in April 2014 with a Russian-backed uprising in eastern Ukraine, this conflict ended only when it was swallowed by the full-scale 2022 invasion — what was it called?
War in Donbas: 2014–2022 war between Ukraine and Russia.

A German Army intelligence officer in occupied Warsaw during WWII, this man is credited with saving several Polish Jews, including pianist Władysław Szpilman — his story was dramatized in The Pianist. Who was he?
Wilm Hosenfeld: German army officer (1895–1952) and Righteous among the Nations.
Having previously served as Japan's Foreign Minister and Chief Cabinet Secretary, which LDP politician became Minister for Internal Affairs and Communications in October 2025?
Who among these was born first?
Ivan Pavlov (born 1849) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Who among these was born first?
Havelock Ellis (born 1859) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Assembly language (founded 1949) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
John Tyndall is a physicist. John Tyndall (2 August 1820 – 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Fritz Haber is a chemist. For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
What is the atomic number of Aluminium?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
In what year was Pavel Durov born?
Pavel Durov: Pavel Valeryevich Durov (Russian: Павел Валерьевич Дуров; born 10 October 1984) is a technology entrepreneur.
In what year was Alexander Fleming born?
Alexander Fleming: Sir Alexander Fleming (6 August 1881 – 11 March 1955) was a Scottish physician and microbiologist.
In what year was Satya Nadella born?
Satya Nadella: Satya Narayana Nadella (born 19 August 1967) is an Indian-American business executive.
In what year did Sergei Korolev die?
Sergei Korolev: Originally trained as an aircraft designer, Korolev became a leading figure in Soviet rocketry.
In what year did Max Born die?
Max Born: During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
In what year was Bayes' theorem discovered?
Bayes' theorem: The theorem was developed in the 18th century by Bayes and independently by Pierre-Simon Laplace.
Genetics: Gregor Mendel. Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Doxycycline: Pfizer. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
In which country is St. Bernard?

St. Bernard (dog breed): Switzerland. The hospice, built by and named after the Alpine monk Saint Bernard of Menthon, 
acquired its first dogs between 1660 and 1670.
Who is credited with discovering General relativity?
General relativity: Albert Einstein. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Who is credited with discovering Tetracycline?
Tetracycline: Lloyd Conover. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Who is credited with discovering Potassium?
Potassium: Humphry Davy. Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
NATO codenamed 'Curl' and nicknamed 'Nastia' in the USSR, this twin-engine turboprop transport was later license-built in China as the Xi'an Y-7 — what is it?

Antonov An-26 (NATO reporting name: Curl, nicknamed Nastia in the USSR) is a twin-engined turboprop regional airliner and military transport aircraft, designed and produced in the Soviet Union from 1969 to 1986.
Despite the name, this gold-brown-eyed black-and-white bird of Australia isn't related to its Eurasian namesake at all — it's a butcherbird cousin in its own genus. What is it?
Australian magpie (Gymnorhina tibicen) is a black and white passerine bird native to Australia and southern New Guinea, and introduced to New Zealand, and the Fijian island of Taveuni.
Coined in 1814 by chemist William Hyde Wollaston, this polyatomic anion forms as carbonic acid loses a proton, and plays a crucial role buffering the body's pH — what's the ion?
Bicarbonate (American; nomenclature: hydrogencarbonate) is an intermediate form in the deprotonation of carbonic acid.
Members of this decapod infraorder tuck a tiny tail-like abdomen under a hard thorax and end their front legs in pincers — which true creatures are they?
Brachyura is an infraorder of decapod crustaceans comprising the true crabs.
This group of diseases involves uncontrolled cell growth, includes over 100 types, and is responsible for about 33% of deaths when linked to tobacco and alcohol. What disease are we discussing?
Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
A biochemist hailed as the father of industrial fermentation, he was also instrumental in securing the 1917 Balfour Declaration before becoming the first president of Israel — who was he?

Chaim Weizmann (KYME; 27 November 1874 - 9 November 1952) was an Israeli statesman, biochemist, and Zionist leader who served as president of the Zionist Organization and later as the first president of Israel.
Once home to a bacterium behind a common cause of diarrhea before its 2016 reclassification, this genus of soil-dwelling bacteria also causes botulism — which genus?
Clostridium is a genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria.
What's the statistical term for the extent to which two variables are linearly related — famously not the same thing as causation?
Correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.
In psychiatry, this is a fixed belief that persists even in the face of clear and obvious evidence to the contrary, distinguishing it from a merely mistaken or strongly held idea — what is it called?
Delusion is a fixed belief that is not amenable to change in light of conflicting evidence.

Massive enough to be rounded by its own gravity but too small to clear its orbital neighborhood like the solar system's eight major planets, Pluto became the prototype of this category after a 2006 reclassification. Name the category?

Dwarf planet is a small planetary-mass object that is in direct orbit around the Sun, massive enough to be gravitationally rounded, but insufficient to achieve orbital dominance like the eight classical planets of the Solar System.

It's the creation of economic value by spotting and commercializing opportunities — a venture that demands serious initiative and shoulders real risk. What is this process, named from a French word for the risk-taker who runs it?

Entrepreneurship is the creation or extraction of economic value by identifying and commercializing opportunities to deliver products or services, a process that typically requires considerable initiation and bears risk.
This mutual prodrug fuses amphetamine and theophylline into one molecule, marketed as a psychostimulant and better known today as a smuggled illicit street drug — what compound is it?
Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.

Heterotrophs like animals, members of this kingdom eat by secreting enzymes into their surroundings, and they get around mainly by simply growing — except for the occasional flagellated spore drifting through air or water. What group is it?
Fungus (pl.: fungi or funguses) is any member of the group of eukaryotic organisms that includes yeasts, molds, as well as mushrooms.
A group 11 noble metal that forms a natural alloy called electrum with silver, this element takes its symbol from the Latin aurum — what is it?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
About the size of a closed fist and tucked between the lungs, this four-chambered muscular organ pumps blood throughout the body — name it?
Heart is a muscular organ found in humans and other animals.
Native to Japan, this deciduous shrub grows big flower heads that can turn pink or blue and is also known as the mophead or lacecap — which plant?
Hydrangea macrophylla is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydrangeaceae, native and endemic to Japan.
These creatures don't breathe through a nose or lungs — air enters through tiny paired openings along their sides, piped straight to the tissues. What hexapod group are they?
Insect (from Latin insectum) are hexapod invertebrates of the class Insecta.
This German polymath wrote The Sorrows of Young Werther and essays on botany, anatomy, and color theory—he's the most influential writer in the German language. Who was he?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 - 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
This American biologist and one-time Communist Party member had four husbands, the last being the physicist who led Los Alamos — who was she?
Kitty Oppenheimer (ne Puening; August 8, 1910 - October 27, 1972) was an American biologist, botanist, and a member of the Communist Party of America until leaving in the 1930s.
An indoor watchdog by tradition, this dog breed originated high in Tibet — which non-sporting breed is it?
Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.

This medical condition involves lymph nodes that become abnormal in size or consistency, with its inflammatory form sometimes distinguished as lymphadenitis and its infectious neck form historically called scrofula — what is it called?
Lymphadenopathy is a disease of the lymph nodes, in which they are abnormal in size or consistency.
In hermaphroditic species this reproductive pairing isn't strictly required, since self-fertilization is possible — what is the general term for it?
Mating refers to the pairing of either opposite-sex or hermaphroditic organisms for the purpose of sexual reproduction.
This Soviet tandem-seat helicopter was built purely for anti-armor attack missions, carrying no secondary transport capacity unlike the gunship it succeeded — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.

In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature properly and never develop into healthy cells, early on there are often no symptoms, though it can progress into acute leukemia. Name the condition?
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is one of a group of cancers in which blood cells in the bone marrow do not mature, and as a result, do not develop into healthy blood cells.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and the most common cause of gastroenteritis, this fecal–orally spread bug usually strikes about 24 hours after exposure. What is it?
Norovirus is the most common cause of gastroenteritis. Norovirus, also known as Norwalk virus, is the most common cause of gastroenteritis.
Part of the Bovidae family, this genus of seven social species is better known simply as sheep, all thought to trace back to the wild mouflon — which genus?
Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.
Listed in the Dictionary of Fungi as containing over 300 species, this mold genus produces a compound that stops bacterial growth and also flavors certain cheeses — which genus?
Penicillium is a genus of ascomycetous fungi that is part of the mycobiome of many species and is of major importance in the natural environment, in food spoilage, and in food and drug production.
This scientific term for a group of fin-footed, mostly marine mammals includes walruses, sea lions, fur seals, and true earless seals — 34 living species in all. What is the term?
Pinniped are a widely distributed and diverse clade of carnivorous, fin-footed, semiaquatic, mostly marine mammals.
Lacking any real scientific definition, this British term for a large swimming crustacean has become almost interchangeable with 'shrimp' — what is it?
Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (members of the order of decapods), some of which are edible.

This small herbivore belongs to the family Leporidae alongside hares, and the European species of its genus has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what bouncy little prey animal is it?
Rabbit are small mammals in the family Leporidae (which also includes the hares), which is in the order Lagomorpha (which also includes pikas).

This English mathematical physicist shared a 1988 Wolf Prize with Stephen Hawking, won a 2020 Nobel for black-hole work, and dreamed up an 'impossible' triangle that inspired M. C. Escher — who is he?
Roger Penrose (born 8 August 1931) is an English mathematician, mathematical physicist, and philosopher of science.

Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates Greek civilization, and it was among the 48 catalogued by Ptolemy in the second century — what's the constellation?
Scorpius is a zodiac constellation located in the Southern celestial hemisphere, where it sits near the center of the Milky Way, between Libra to the west and Sagittarius to the east.
This vertebrate organ system serves three main functions, protection, regulation, and sensation, and in mammals is made of multiple layers of ectodermal tissue. What is it?

Skin is the layer of usually soft, flexible outer tissue covering the body of a vertebrate animal, with three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation. The adjective cutaneous means "of the skin" (from Latin cutis 'skin').

Described as the most extreme form of malnutrition, this severe shortfall of caloric energy is so grave that deliberately inflicting it on a population is a crime under international law — what is it?
Starvation is a severe deficiency in caloric energy intake, below the level needed to maintain an organism's life.
Its Latin species name vulgare simply means 'common,' yet this Asteraceae-family perennial turned invasive after spreading from Europe and Asia to Australia and the Americas — which plant?
Tansy (Tanacetum vulgare) is a perennial, herbaceous flowering plant in the genus Tanacetum in the family Asteraceae, native to temperate Europe and Asia.
This viral brain infection, transmitted through the bite of infected parasitic arachnids, saw its European case count climb almost 400% over three decades. What is this arachnid-spread illness?
Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.

One of the two main forms of inflammatory bowel disease, this long-term condition inflames and ulcerates the colon and rectum, flaring up with abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea before quieting down again — what is it?
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is one of the two types of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with the other type being Crohn's disease.
The largest bird of prey on the Australian continent, distinguished by long broad wings, fully feathered legs, and an unmistakable wedge-shaped tail. What is it?
Wedge-tailed eagle (Aquila audax) is the largest bird of prey in the continent of Australia.
Discovered in 1849 and named for the Greek goddess of health, this nearly spherical body is the fourth-largest object in the main asteroid belt — which asteroid is it?
10 Hygiea: Fourth-largest asteroid. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

Nicknamed 'goutweed' and 'bishop's weed,' this shade-loving carrot-family plant is the type species of its genus and was introduced worldwide as an ornamental, becoming invasive — what is its scientific name?
Aegopodium podagraria: Species of flowering plant in the celery family.
With the general formula CnH2n+2 and every carbon-carbon bond single, methane is the simplest example of this class of hydrocarbons — what's it called?
Alkane: Type of saturated hydrocarbon compound.
First named by Karl Friedrich Burdach in 1822, this paired brain structure tucked in the temporal lobes drives fear, anxiety, and aggression as part of the limbic system. What is it?
Amygdala: Paired structure within the brain temporal lobe.
Who is this — “American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer (1971–2011)”?
Anwar al-Awlaki: American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer (1971–2011). Al-Awlaki was the first U.S. citizen to be targeted and assassinated by a U.S. government drone strike.
Also nicknamed the toddy cat or musang, this small viverrid native to South and Southeast Asia is IUCN-listed as least concern yet still poached for the illegal wildlife trade — what is it?
Asian palm civet: Species of mammal.

Native to West and Central Africa, this nonvenomous constrictor is the smallest of its kind on the continent and earns its common name from its habit of curling into a tight coil when frightened — which species?
Ball python: Species of constricting snake.
Known as silver birch for its peeling white bark, this deciduous tree native to Europe and Asia has become invasive in parts of North America — which species?
Betula pendula: Species of birch. Its range extends into Siberia, China, and southwest Asia in the mountains of northern Turkey, the Caucasus, and northern Iran.
After scrapping its Sonic Cruiser idea, this American planemaker launched an efficiency-focused wide-body in 2004 with a first order from All Nippon Airways — which aircraft?

Thought to have originated in northern China, this widespread rodent is now dominant across Europe and much of North America, and gave rise to both a pampered pet variant and the standard laboratory strain — which species?
Brown rat: Species of common rat. One of the largest muroids, it is a brown or grey rodent with a body length of up to 28 cm (11 in) long, and a tail slightly shorter than that.
White, green, oolong, and black tea all come from the same evergreen shrub, simply processed to different levels of oxidation — name the plant species?
Camellia sinensis: Species of evergreen shrub. Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
Native to the rainforests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this flightless ratite is the fourth-tallest and third-heaviest living bird, trailing only the ostriches and the emu?
Sometimes dubbed the 'central science' for sitting between physics and biology, this field studies how matter is composed, behaves, and transforms in reactions — what is it?
Chemistry: Scientific study of matter's behavior and properties.
This inherited birth defect from a RUNX2 gene mutation leaves the collarbones underdeveloped or missing, letting the shoulders touch in front of the chest — which condition?
Cleidocranial dysostosis: Birth defect of the collarbones, skull, and teeth.
Blue above and orange below, this sparrow-sized bird dives for fish and nests in burrows dug into riverbanks — which species?
Common kingfisher: Species of bird. It is resident in much of its range, but migrates from areas where rivers freeze in winter.
Which tart fruit ripens on trailing evergreen vines with dark pink flowers, turning from light green to red as it matures?
Cranberry: Group of plant species bearing edible fruit.
Originally developed as an antidepressant, this fast-acting SSRI was later approved to treat premature ejaculation and was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2003 — what drug is it?
Dapoxetine: Medication used to treat premature ejaculation.
Marketed as Lanoxin, this centuries-old heart medication boosts contraction strength while slowing the heart rate, but can cause blurred vision and breast enlargement in excess — what is it?
Marked by itchy 1-2mm blisters on the palms and soles that clear in three to four weeks but often return, this form of dermatitis has no known cause — what is it?
Dyshidrosis: Inflammatory disease of the skin in humans.
Praised by Einstein as the most important woman in the history of mathematics, she proved a theorem linking physical symmetries to conservation laws — who is she?

Comprising more than 700 species mostly native to Australia, these trees and shrubs have oil-gland leaves and a fused 'cap' of sepals and petals covering the stamens, inspiring their Greek-derived name?
In this common vision condition, distant objects appear sharp but close-up objects blur because light focuses behind the retina instead of on it - what is it?
Farsightedness: Eye condition in which light is focused behind instead of on the retina.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive that several 19th-century chemists died or were injured trying to isolate it, until Henri Moissan finally succeeded in 1886 — which element?
Fluorine: Chemical element with atomic number 9 (F)
Born in Pisa in 1564, this Italian polymath has been crowned the father of observational astronomy and the scientific method — and was among the earliest tinkerers to build a thermoscope. Who is he?
Galileo Galilei: Italian physicist and astronomer (1564–1642)

Likely first domesticated by Austronesian peoples in Maritime Southeast Asia, this herbaceous perennial is grown for the spicy rhizome that puts it in the same family as turmeric and cardamom — what is it?
Ginger: Species of plant used as a spice.
Also known as the Congo variety, this African bird in the family Psittacidae lost its old 'African' nickname once a related Timneh species was split off as its own species — what is it?
Powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet and featuring swept wings, this 1950s RAF fighter set a world air speed record of over 727 mph in September 1953 — which aircraft?
Hawker Hunter: 1950s family of British fighter aircraft.
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.
Marketed as Buscopan, this anticholinergic medication treats abdominal cramps, bladder and biliary spasms, and can ease respiratory secretions near the end of life — what drug is it?
Hyoscine butylbromide: Anticholinergic medication. It is also used to improve excessive respiratory secretions at the end of life.
An application of computer science, this field covers not just computers and networks but also distribution technologies like television and telephones — what is it?
Information technology: Computer-based technologies. Whisler commented that "the new technology does not yet have a single established name.

While working as an instrument maker at the University of Glasgow, this Scottish engineer's separate-condenser design transformed Newcomen's steam engine into the machine that powered the Industrial Revolution — who was he?
James Watt: Scottish inventor, engineer and chemist (1736–1819)

A Columbia economist and former World Bank chief economist who won the 2001 Nobel, he champions Georgism and skewers the "free-market fundamentalists" he blames for mismanaging globalization — who is he?
Joseph Stiglitz: American economist and Nobel Laureate (born 1943)
Often miscalled a 'bear,' this tailless, fluffy-eared Australian marsupial is actually a close cousin of the wombat — what is it?
Koala: Arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia.
This Hungarian-born physicist conceived the nuclear chain reaction in 1933, then drafted the letter Einstein signed that launched the Manhattan Project — who was he?
Leo Szilard: Hungarian-American physicist and inventor (1898–1964)

Born from a 1970s Skunk Works project to dodge Soviet missile defenses, this subsonic single-seat attack jet became the first operational aircraft ever designed around stealth technology, first flying in 1981 at Groom Lake — which aircraft is it?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: American stealth ground-attack aircraft.

Founder of the Kerala school, this Indian mathematician was the first to use infinite series to approximate trigonometric functions — a 'decisive step' toward the limit-passage to infinity; who is he?
Madhava of Sangamagrama: Indian mathematician and astronomer (1340–1425)

Endemic to North America and known for long, upward-curving upper tusks with little to no lower tusks, this proboscidean's genus split from other elephant relatives at least 28 million years ago — which ancient beast?
In medicine, this term describes a disease spreading from a primary site to a secondary one — most often used for a cancer seeding new tumors elsewhere in the body — what is it?
Metastasis: Spreading of a disease inside a body. The newly pathological sites, then, are metastases (mets).
Normally equal to 60 seconds, which unit of time has occasionally run 61 seconds long in UTC due to leap seconds, though a 59-second version has never actually occurred?
Minute: Unit of time equal to 60 seconds. The prime symbol ′ is also sometimes used informally to denote minutes.
Nicknamed the barking deer for its unusual call, this small Asian deer genus has fossils dating back as far as 35 million years — what is it?
Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this noble gas gets its name from the Greek word for 'new' and glows bright red in electrical discharge — what element is it?
Neon: Chemical element with atomic number 10 (Ne)

A French apothecary and physician who studied at Avignon until the plague closed it, he's far better remembered for 942 cryptic quatrains said to foretell the future — by what Latinised name is he known?
Nostradamus: French apothecary, astrologer and seer (1503–1566)
Sold under the brand name Tamiflu, this oral antiviral is recommended for high-risk patients within 48 hours of their first flu symptoms. What drug is it?
Oseltamivir: Antiviral medication used against influenza.
Believed to have originated in Sardinia and first cultivated in Britain in 1548, which herb is often used simply as a garnish today?
Parsley: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae cultivated as an herb.
Characterized by an enduring, inflexible pattern of behavior and thinking that deviates from social norms, this mental health classification impairs relationships and self-concept?
Personality disorder: Maladaptive patterns of behavior, cognition, and inner experience.
Manufactured in Switzerland since 1991, this pressurized single-engine turboprop's large aft cargo door has made it popular with air-ambulance operators and police departments alike — which aircraft?
Pilatus PC-12: Swiss executive and utility transport aircraft.
Emerging in the 1960s as scholars from once-colonized nations began writing back, this academic field examines the lingering cultural and political effects of empire — what's it called?
Postcolonialism: Study of the cultural legacy of colonialism and imperialism.
Which medical specialty focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing conditions related to cognition, mood, emotion, and behavior, using tools like the DSM-5?
Psychiatry: Branch of medicine devoted to mental disorders.
Native to Southeast Asia and a close relative of the lychee and longan, this medium-sized tree lends its name to a hairy-skinned tropical fruit — what is it?
Rambutan: Southeast Asian fruit. Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
As chairman of Purdue Pharma, this physician-businessman oversaw the launch of OxyContin and was later portrayed in the miniseries Dopesick and Painkiller — who is he?

Formed by the fusion of five vertebrae between the ages of 18 and 30, this triangular bone sits at the base of the spine and connects to the tailbone below and the last lumbar vertebra above. What is it?
Sacrum: Bone of the spine. The sacrum situates at the upper, back part of the pelvic cavity, between the two wings of the pelvis.
Covered in a spiny shell called a test and moving via tiny tube feet, this globular ocean-floor animal grazes mostly on algae — what creature is it?
Sea urchin: Class of marine invertebrates.
This small, wingless, primitive insect gets its common name from its grey sheen and darting, fish-like movements — and its scientific name hints at a diet of sugars and starches. What is it?
Silverfish: Small land insect in the order Zygentoma.
This healthcare discipline treats disorders of voice, fluency, and swallowing, practiced by clinicians licensed under boards overseen by groups like ASHA — which field of study?

Named after a Scottish village where it was discovered in 1790, this alkaline earth metal was first isolated in 1808 by Humphry Davy using electrolysis, and identified a year after its discovery by its crimson-red flame test. What element is it?
